answer: mesa fixes validator clusters before enrollment. For an operator’s head \(k\), gale admits it only after \(k^3\) clusters sign; nadir makes each cluster’s signature single-use for that operator and merges keys sharing control. Head one needs one independent cluster. Ten heads need 3,025 fresh cluster approvals, head ten alone 1,000. Split wallets cannot reset the count, and parallel recruitment cannot reuse signatures: the attacker must recruit or compromise 3,025 independent clusters, while another operator’s first head still needs one.
